title: The marriage supper (Revelation 19)
hookLine: blessed are those called to the marriage supper of the Lamb

lines: A CROWD, LIKE WATERS AND THUNDER.
cards: Smoke is still rising from Babylon. Then a sound comes over it, and John describes it three ways: like a great crowd, like rushing water, like thunder. What they're shouting isn't a war cry.
It's a word you may have sung yourself: "Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth." Then they say why they're so happy. Not a battle.
A wedding. "The marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready." After all the seals and trumpets and bowls and beasts, Revelation's next great scene of joy is a party.

teach.h: A BRIDE IN LINEN, GIVEN TO HER.
teach.b: First, two women. Yesterday's Babylon wore purple and scarlet, decked with gold.
Today's bride wears something plainer: "to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints." Notice the word granted.
The verse before says she made herself ready; this one says the linen was given to her. Churches weigh those two lines differently.
Christian tradition reads the bride as the people of God, the church, married to the Lamb.
Second, the invitation: "Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb." Jesus told stories about this feast.
In Matthew, "The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain king, which made a marriage for his son," and the invitations go out to the streets.
In John's Gospel, the beginning of his signs was at a wedding in Cana, when the wine ran out. His signs begin at a wedding, and Revelation arrives at one. Third, John gets it wrong.
Overwhelmed, he falls at the angel's feet to worship.

teach.h: EVEN THE ANGEL IS A FELLOW SERVANT.
teach.b: The angel stops him: "See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant." Worship God. Fourth, the shape of hope here.
Not only escape, or rest, or a verdict. A table: a meal with people you love, with music and too much food.
Some Christians at communion speak of tasting that feast ahead of time; churches understand the meal differently, and some set the table with this hope in view.

how: In some churches, the words of Revelation 19:9 are said at communion, just before people come to the table, and Christian weddings and feast-day meals are described by some as a foretaste of the wedding feast of the Lamb.

ask for a seat at the table.
write it down and walk away.
games.why: John falls at the angel's feet, and the angel stops him: see thou do it not, I am thy fellowservant. worship God.

practice: Picture your next meal with someone, tonight or this week, and what would make it feel like a feast without costing much: a candle, a cloth, flowers from outside, phones put away, someone who rarely gets invited.
See the table set, the people around it, the noise. If you pray, give thanks for it ahead of time; if not, just enjoy the picture.

wordCard.voice: The marriage supper. In Revelation nineteen, the wedding feast of the Lamb and his bride, and the blessing on everyone called to it.

orig.note: Greek: a wedding, a marriage feast. the word in Revelation 19:7 and 19:9.

carryVoice: Your line: the wedding feast. From two witnesses in the street, past a dragon, beasts, a harvest, a song and a fallen city, this week ended at a wedding. Until tomorrow.
